reason: RIGHT keeps axis-labelled, gridlined charts and a four-card KPI row that stay legible at phone width, while LEFT leaves an orphaned fifth KPI card on desktop and shrinks chart labels to near-unreadable size on the phone.

RIGHT uses a clean line chart plus an in-cell bar table that works on desktop and phone, whereas LEFT's 14-bar chart has overlapping value labels colliding with the dashed average line and is cropped to eight days on the phone with tiny weekday/weekend chart text.

On the phone RIGHT keeps a compact table and a readable rainfall bar chart (though one x-label is missing), while LEFT turns the county table into six long repeated stacked cards; LEFT's desktop scatter plot is nice but does not outweigh that.

RIGHT has a full-width stacked favorable/neutral/unfavorable bar chart with readable labels and a diverging change chart on desktop, versus LEFT's table with huge KPI cards and a truncated-label grouped bar chart; both phone versions are card-heavy with some tiny chart text.

RIGHT's margin-trend chart is larger, with big value labels on every point and a trailing-four-quarters row in the table, while LEFT's chart is small with only one labeled point; both degrade to stacked cards on the phone.
LEFT reads like a finished press release with serif body text, an italic deck, a labelled key-facts panel and a contact card, whereas RIGHT is a plainer generic KPI-plus-bullets layout.
RIGHT gives stronger hierarchy with stat cards for the $500 and $40 amounts and a boxed purchase list, while LEFT is tidy with numbered steps but flatter and plainer.

RIGHT has a larger serif lead paragraph, more generous spacing, serif subheads matching the body and a numbered list for the advice, giving a more refined long-read than LEFT's sans subheads over small serif text.

LEFT's single worked-example table stays compact and readable on the phone, while RIGHT's proportion bar has tiny illegible labels at 400px and its tier and calculation tables become eight verbose stacked cards, despite the nicer desktop bar.

LEFT has a warmer, more polished feel with a green highlighted date panel, a solid filled timeline with bold times, a boxed getting-here list and a letter sign-off, versus RIGHT's plainer hollow-dot timeline and generic KPI cards.
